papers.title: Fly-JEPA: Learning Dynamics Via Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures for Aerial Robots
papers.authors: Rao, Pratyaksh; Loianno, Giuseppe
papers.affiliations: UC Berkeley; UC Berkeley
papers.summary: Fly-JEPA learns action-conditioned aerial-robot dynamics in a compact embedding space. Multi-step self-supervised prediction encourages the representation to retain information useful for future motion. The approach accepts different observation modalities, and the authors investigate the benefit of a depth-pretrained visual encoder on real aerial robots.
papers.why: Compact action-conditioned latent dynamics with multi-step self-supervision. A particularly close bridge between your current predictive-model work and your history in autonomous drones. Prioritize the remaining poster; the oral has passed.
papers.question: What latent size and rollout horizon preserve control performance, and what is the full onboard latency?

papers.title: Shallow-π: Knowledge Distillation for Flow-Based VLAs
papers.authors: Jeon, Boseong; Choi, Yunho; Kim, Taehan
papers.affiliations: 42dot; Seoul National University; Samsung Research
papers.summary: Shallow-π distills both the visual-language backbone and flow-based action head into a shallower policy. Reducing transformer depth from 18 layers to six targets the cost of on-device inference. The authors report faster inference with a small change in task success and evaluate deployment on Jetson hardware across several robot platforms.
papers.why: Compresses both the VLM backbone and flow action head from 18 to 6 layers. The abstract reports more than 2× inference speedup and under one percentage point success loss, with Jetson experiments. Strong practical compression reference for an efficient world-action model.
papers.question: Which loss preserves action modes, and what are batch-one latency, memory, and power on Orin?

papers.title: CLAM: Continuous Latent Action Models for Robot Learning from Unlabeled Demonstrations
papers.authors: Liang, Anthony; Czempin, Pavel; Hong, Matthew; Zhou, Yutai; Wang, Jingzhen; Bıyık, Erdem; Tu, Stephen
papers.affiliations: University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California
papers.summary: CLAM learns continuous latent actions from observation-only demonstrations. A jointly learned decoder connects those latent actions to executable robot commands using a relatively small amount of action-labeled play data. Continuous action representations are intended to retain fine motor detail that can be lost through discretization.
papers.why: Learns continuous latent actions using self-supervised dynamics, then uses a small action-labeled play set to connect them to robot control. Directly relevant to ModAR and 3PoinTr, especially the interface between actionless video and executable actions.
papers.question: What fixes latent-action identifiability, and how much labeled play is needed under an embodiment change?

papers.title: Trajectory-Based Diffusion from One‑shot Human Video for Generalizable Manipulation
papers.authors: Pan, Guoping; Yu, Xinmiao; Cao, Wannan; Jiang, Baolin; Li, Yizhe; Cheng, Yi; Liu, Houde
papers.affiliations: Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; University of Science and Technology of China; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; Shenzhen Graduate School, Tsinghua University
papers.summary: This method learns transferable manipulation behavior from a single human demonstration video. Object-centric 6D trajectories provide an intermediate representation between human motion and robot actions. A trajectory-based diffusion policy uses this representation to reduce visual-domain and embodiment differences during transfer.
papers.why: Uses object trajectories as an interface between one-shot human video and manipulation. A close comparison for your use of geometric motion as transferable supervision. Adjacent to CLAM at the poster session, making this an efficient pair of conversations.
papers.question: How are occluded object motion and 6D pose uncertainty handled before policy learning?

papers.title: DreamMimic: Learning Visuomotor Whole-Body Loco-Manipulation Via World Model
papers.authors: Yin, Jie; Lai, Xingyu
papers.affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Tsinghua University
papers.summary: DreamMimic uses a recurrent state-space world model to support visuomotor whole-body locomotion and manipulation. Predictive latent dynamics and auxiliary object/contact information help transfer behavior from a privileged teacher to a deployable student policy. The world model serves as a learning aid rather than necessarily running a planner at every control step.
papers.why: Uses predictive latent dynamics to support teacher–student transfer for whole-body behavior. Useful for studying which predictive heads actually improve a deployed policy.
papers.question: Which predictive losses matter for transfer, and which parts of the world model remain at inference?

papers.title: DAWN: Noise-Robust Quadruped Parkour Via Depth-Denoising World Models
papers.authors: Choi, Yohan; Kim, Min-Jun; Kim, Jin-Sung; Kim, Yong-Jae; Han, Youn-Hee
papers.affiliations: Korea University of Technology and Education; Korea University of Technology and Education; Korea University of Technology and Education; Korea University of Technology and Education; Korea University of Technology and Education
papers.summary: DAWN trains a world model to make quadruped parkour robust to noisy depth observations. It combines a noisy-input encoder, clean-depth reconstruction, and contrastive latent alignment. The learned representation is used for locomotion with raw depth, with the authors reporting transfer to a physical quadruped without extra deployment-time computation.
papers.why: Noisy-input encoding, clean-depth reconstruction, and latent alignment support robust locomotion. The claim of no additional inference cost makes this a useful example of predictive training objectives improving a small deployed controller.
papers.question: Does it remain robust to depth failure modes absent from training, and which modules run on the robot?

papers.title: eVGGT: An Efficient Geometry-Aware Vision Encoder for Visuomotor Policies
papers.authors: Vuong, An Dinh; Vu, Minh Nhat; Reid, Ian
papers.leadAuthors: Vuong, An Dinh;  Vu, Minh Nhat
papers.affiliations: MBZUAI; VinUni; University of Adelaide
papers.summary: eVGGT distills a geometric vision model into an efficient encoder for visuomotor policies. The encoder supplies spatial features to imitation-learning methods such as ACT and Diffusion Policy. Experiments study the tradeoff between geometric representation quality, memory use, inference speed, and manipulation success under changing viewpoints.
papers.why: A distilled geometry encoder integrated into ACT and Diffusion Policy. The abstract reports nearly 5× speedup and 63% less memory than its geometry-aware comparison encoders. This is one of the closest matches to your MASt3R/DUSt3R experience and efficiency goal.
papers.question: Which geometric capabilities survive compression, and is the bottleneck encoder latency or action generation?

papers.title: PC-VLA: A Sub-Million Parameter Predictive-Coding Policy for Language-Conditioned Robot Manipulation
papers.authors: Sawada, Hiroki; Kasahara, Shunichi
papers.affiliations: Sony Computer Science Laboratories, Inc
papers.summary: PC-VLA pairs a frozen vision-language frontend with a small trainable recurrent policy. Its hierarchy predicts observations, proprioception, and actions at multiple time scales, while online latent-state optimization incorporates sensory prediction errors. LIBERO experiments study predictive coding as an alternative to large trainable action models. The frozen frontend is excluded from the sub-million parameter count.
papers.why: A 0.676M-parameter trainable recurrent policy predicts visual, proprioceptive, and action signals, with online latent error correction. Particularly interesting as a small recurrent alternative to a large autoregressive policy.
papers.question: What is total frontend-plus-policy latency, including online error regression, and does it work on physical robots?

papers.title: TrackDeform3D: Markerless and Autonomous 3D Keypoint Tracking and Dataset Collection for Deformable Objects
papers.authors: Zong, Yeheng; Chen, Yizhou; Chia-Tung, Yang; Bowler, Alexander; Vasudevan, Ram
papers.affiliations: University of Michigan; University of Michigan, Ann Arbor; University of michigan; University of Michigan; University of Michigan
papers.summary: TrackDeform3D collects markerless deformable-object trajectories using RGB-D cameras. Motion-consistency constraints encourage temporally smooth, geometrically coherent 3D keypoint tracks. The authors evaluate tracking across object categories and introduce a dataset with six deformable objects, aiming to reduce the annotation and motion-capture burden for dynamics research.
papers.why: RGB-D keypoint trajectories with motion-consistency constraints and a deformable-object dataset. A concrete data and evaluation connection for PointZero and DeformGS.
papers.question: Can the dataset test persistent dense tracks through severe deformation and occlusion?

papers.title: Object Reconstruction under Occlusion with Generative Priors and Contact-Induced Constraints
papers.authors: Zhu, Minghan; Wang, Zhiyi; Sun, Qihang; Ghaffari, Maani; Posa, Michael
papers.affiliations: University of Michigan; University of Michigan; University of Michigan, Ann Arbor; University of Michigan; University of Pennsylvania
papers.summary: The method reconstructs partially observed objects by combining learned generative shape priors with sparse constraints from contact. Contact-guided generation reduces uncertainty about hidden boundaries when additional camera viewpoints are unavailable. The paper compares guidance strategies and evaluates reconstruction with synthetic and real observations.
papers.why: Combines generative shape completion with sparse contact constraints. Closely matches RaySt3R-style completion while adding interaction evidence that a world model can exploit.
papers.question: Can uncertainty over hidden geometry be retained for planning instead of committing to one completed shape?

papers.title: Test-Time Spatial Reasoning for Robot Manipulation Using Generative Real-to-Sim
papers.authors: Kapelyukh, Ivan; Hu, Yafei; Gong, Ran; May, Brandon; Kusnur, Tushar; Herlant, Laura; Schmeckpeper, Karl; Johns, Edward; Zhang, Xiaohan
papers.affiliations: Imperial College London; Robotics and AI Institute; UCLA; RAI Institute; Robotics and AI Institute; Boston Dynamics AI Institute; Robotics and AI Institute; Imperial College London; SUNY Binghamton
papers.summary: Simify turns an RGB-D observation into a completed simulation scene using generative models. It then performs large-scale parallel physics rollouts and searches for useful manipulation behavior at test time. The approach uses reconstructed geometry and explicit simulation to support spatial reasoning and rearrangement without requiring every transition to be predicted by a video model.
papers.why: Simify completes an RGB-D scene into simulation assets and searches physics rollouts for manipulation. It makes the geometry-to-planning connection explicit and provides a useful alternative to learning every transition inside a video model.
papers.question: What fraction of wall-clock time is reconstruction versus rollout search, and which contact errors dominate?

papers.title: AtomVLA: Scalable Post-Training for Robotic Manipulation via Predictive Latent World Models
papers.authors: Sun, Xiaoquan; XU, ZETIAN; Cao, Chen; Liu, Zonghe; Sun, Yihan; Pang, Jingrui; Zhang, Ruijian; Yang, Zhen; Pang, Kang; He, Dingxin; Yuan, Mingqi; Chen, Jiayu
papers.affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology; THE UNIVERSITY OF HONG KONG; The University of Hong Kong; The University of Hong Kong; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Tsinghua University; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Beihang University; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Huazhong University of Science & Technology; The Hong Kong Polytechnic University; The University of Hong Kong
papers.summary: AtomVLA decomposes long manipulation tasks into smaller subtasks and uses a pretrained latent world model to evaluate candidate action chunks. These scores support offline GRPO post-training, reducing reliance on expensive online robot rollouts. Experiments examine long-horizon robustness in simulation and physical manipulation.
papers.why: Uses a predictive latent world model to score action chunks for offline policy post-training. A direct connection to ModAR: use prediction to improve action selection without paying for new physical rollouts.
papers.question: How do model errors bias GRPO, and how does success vary with latent rollout horizon and inference cost?

papers.title: ZeroBot: Learning from Scratch in Minutes with Generative Real2Sim
papers.authors: Kapelyukh, Ivan; Zhang, Xiaohan; James, Stephen; Herlant, Laura; Johns, Edward
papers.affiliations: Imperial College London; Binghamton University; Imperial College London; Boston Dynamics AI Institute; Imperial College London
papers.summary: ZeroBot creates an object mesh from a single image and uses the generated geometry for parallel simulation-based reinforcement learning. Its action representation emphasizes robot-object contact to accelerate learning. The system is evaluated on physical manipulation without demonstration data, pretrained policies, or a supplied object model.
papers.why: Builds simulation from one image and learns a contact-informed manipulation policy. A strong comparison for deciding when pretrained geometry plus a simulator is cheaper than a large learned world model.
papers.question: Does the reported training time include image-to-3D generation, simulator setup, and all search costs?

papers.title: SparseWorld: Enhancing End-To-End Autonomous Driving Via World Models with Sparse Scene Representation
papers.authors: Wang, Ruoyu; Wang, Jingke; Ma, Yukai; Huang, Yuehao; Lei, Shuangming; Xu, Guanglin; Ye, Aixue; Liu, Yong
papers.affiliations: Zhejiang University; Zhejiang University; Zhejiang University; Zhejiang University; Zhejiang University; Huawei; 2012 Labs, Huawei; Zhejiang University
papers.summary: SparseWorld predicts future map elements and nearby agents in a sparse latent representation for driving. Temporal and spatial attention support autoregressive rollout, and the anticipated state informs motion prediction and planning. The method is evaluated on driving benchmarks; applying the same sparse-state principle to manipulation remains an open question.
papers.why: Predicts sparse map and agent representations rather than dense future video. Worth attending for the representation choice: predict only state that improves downstream decisions.
papers.question: What fails when interaction-relevant state is missing from the sparse representation, and could contact geometry fit?

papers.title: Motion-Focused Latent Action Enables Cross-Embodiment VLA Training from Human EgoVideos
papers.authors: XU, RUNZE; Zhang, Yiluo; Wang, Jian; Wang, Yu; Yu, Jincheng
papers.affiliations: Tsinghua University; Tianfu Jiangxi Laboratory; Tsinghua Univ.; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University
papers.summary: This framework extracts motion-focused latent actions from unlabeled human egocentric video. A disentangled VQ-VAE separates action dynamics from visual background, while physical masks support a shared action codebook. Adaptation separates predicted intent from current visual state so that robot-specific action generation can use limited labeled trajectories.
papers.why: Disentangles motion from background in a latent action codebook, pretrains on unlabeled human video, then adapts with robot trajectories. A close comparison to 3PoinTr and ModAR.
papers.question: Do the masks discard subtle contact motion, and how much adaptation data is needed outside the tested embodiments?

papers.title: CRAFT: Video Diffusion for Bimanual Robot Data Generation
papers.authors: Chen, Jason; Liu, I-Chun Arthur; Sukhatme, Gaurav; Seita, Daniel
papers.affiliations: University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California; University of Southern California
papers.summary: CRAFT generates visually diverse bimanual demonstrations with video diffusion. Simulator trajectories provide structural edge conditions and action labels; generation varies appearance, viewpoints, object placement, and embodiment. The work tests whether these augmented videos improve learned manipulation behavior while reducing the need to replay every demonstration on physical robots.
papers.why: Conditions video diffusion on simulation-derived edge structure, retaining action labels from the simulated trajectories. Highly relevant to using strong video priors while keeping generated data tied to robot actions.
papers.question: How do you detect generated object motion that violates the retained action labels?

papers.title: Vision-Conditioned Variational Bayesian Last Layer Dynamics Models
papers.authors: Brunzema, Paul; Lew, Thomas; Zhang, Ray; Shirasawa, Takeru; Subosits, John; Greiff, Marcus
papers.affiliations: RWTH Aachen University; Toyota Research Institute; University of Michigan; Toyota Research Institute; Toyota Research Institute; Toyota Research Institute
papers.summary: A vision-conditioned Bayesian last-layer model anticipates changes in system dynamics from visual context. The model adapts latent features with affine transformations and supplies predictions to an optimal controller. Vehicle-racing experiments with varying surface conditions test whether visual cues can enable proactive adaptation before a purely reactive controller detects the change.
papers.why: Visual context conditions a lightweight dynamics adaptation mechanism, demonstrated in a vehicle encountering varying surface conditions. Useful for separating fast environment adaptation from expensive full-model updating.
papers.question: Which uncertainty is calibrated, and can the visual conditioning anticipate changes in contact dynamics?

papers.title: D3P: Dynamic Denoising Diffusion Policy Via Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Yu, Shu'ang; Gao, Feng; Wu, Yi; Yu, Chao; Wang, Yu
papers.affiliations: Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University
papers.summary: D3P learns how many denoising steps a diffusion policy should spend on each action. A state-aware adaptor uses reinforcement learning to balance computation against task performance. The paper evaluates dynamic compute allocation in simulation and real manipulation, providing an alternative to a fixed denoising budget.
papers.why: Allocates denoising steps dynamically with a learned adaptor. Compare this with fixed one-step distillation: it may spend compute only where an action needs it. Reported speedups are 2.2× in simulation and 1.9× on the real setup.
papers.question: Is worst-case reaction latency bounded, and does the adaptor cost erase gains on embedded hardware?

papers.title: Training Fast Robot Policies with Slow Foundation Models
papers.authors: Singh, Utsav; Bhattacharyya, Pramit; Namboodiri, Vinay; Bedi, Amrit Singh
papers.affiliations: University of Central Florida; Indian Institute of Technology, Kanpur; University of Bath; University of Maryland, College Park
papers.summary: This work uses slow foundation models during training to improve a faster deployable robot policy. Vision-language analysis of failures informs language-model-generated reward construction, which guides policy learning. Expensive reasoning is kept outside the deployed control loop while the small policy benefits from training-time feedback.
papers.why: Uses foundation-model analysis of failures and reward construction to improve a lightweight policy during training. A useful deployment design where expensive reasoning can remain off the robot.
papers.question: What is total training cost per success improvement, and how much human intervention remains?

papers.title: Canonical Policy: Learning Canonical 3D Representation for SE(3)-Equivariant Policy
papers.authors: Zhang, Zhiyuan; Xu, Zhengtong; Lakamsani, Jai; She, Yu
papers.affiliations: Purdue University; Purdue University; Purdue University; Purdue University
papers.summary: Canonical Policy maps point-cloud observations into a canonical geometric representation before action generation. Its framework connects this canonicalization to SE(3)-equivariant policy learning, aiming to improve transfer across object configurations, camera viewpoints, and spatial transformations. The authors evaluate simulated and real manipulation tasks.
papers.why: Canonicalizes point-cloud observations to structure equivariant imitation learning. A good comparison for how much geometric invariance should be built in versus learned by a large model.
papers.question: When does canonicalization become ambiguous, and how does that affect multimodal actions?

papers.title: VLASH: Real-Time VLAs Via Future-State-Aware Asynchronous Inference
papers.authors: Tang, Jiaming; Sun, Yufei; Zhao, Yilong; Yang, Shang; Lin, Yujun; Zhang, Zhuoyang; Hou, James; Lu, Yao; Liu, Zhijian; Han, Song
papers.affiliations: MIT; Tsinghua University; UC Berkeley; Massachusetts Institute of Technology; NVIDIA; MIT; California Institute of Technology; Physical Intelligence; UC San Diego; Massachusetts Institute of Technology
papers.summary: VLASH overlaps policy inference with action execution. It estimates the robot state at the future execution time using the previous action chunk, reducing the mismatch that otherwise destabilizes asynchronous control. Experiments investigate reaction delay, motion continuity, and fast dynamic manipulation without adding a separate costly inference module.
papers.why: Rolls the robot state forward with the previous action chunk to align asynchronous inference with execution time. Important because reducing reaction delay can matter more than merely making a forward pass faster.
papers.question: How are model error and action interruption handled when the environment moves unexpectedly?

papers.title: Scaling Cross-Embodiment World Models for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.authors: He, Zihao; Ai, Bo; Mu, Tongzhou; Liu, Yulin; Wan, Weikang; Fu, Jiawei; Du, Yilun; Christensen, Henrik Iskov; Su, Hao
papers.affiliations: Shanghai Jiao Tong University; University of California San Diego; UC San Diego; UCSD; University of California, San Diego; University of California San Diego; MIT; UC San Diego; UCSD
papers.summary: This world model represents human and robot hands as sets of 3D particles and actions as particle displacement fields. A graph model learns interactions from diverse simulated robots and real human data, then supports model-predictive control on new hands. Rigid and deformable manipulation experiments examine how embodiment diversity and mixed data affect transfer.
papers.why: My strongest paper recommendation. Represents human and robot hands as 3D particles, actions as particle displacements, and learns graph dynamics for MPC across embodiments. This connects exceptionally well to PointZero and your use of geometric tracks for action transfer.
papers.question: Can PointZero-like dense tracks supply the particle state? What breaks with occlusion, contact, or unseen deformables?

papers.title: GrndCtrl: Grounding World Models Via Self-Supervised Reward Alignment
papers.authors: He, Haoyang; Patrikar, Jay; Kim, Dong Ki; Smith, Max; McGann, Daniel; Agha-mohammadi, Ali-akbar; Omidshafiei, Shayegan; Scherer, Sebastian
papers.affiliations: FieldAI; Carnegie Mellon University; Massachusetts Institute of Tech.; FieldAI; Carnegie Mellon University; NASA-JPL, Caltech; Field AI, Inc.; Carnegie Mellon University
papers.summary: GrndCtrl post-trains generative world models with self-supervised geometric rewards. Pose cycle consistency, depth reprojection, and temporal coherence supply feedback to a GRPO-based alignment procedure. The goal is to improve spatially stable rollouts and navigation behavior beyond what visual realism or supervised fine-tuning alone provides.
papers.why: Post-trains a generative world model using geometric rewards such as pose cycles and depth reprojection. A direct line of inquiry for Atlas and Modality Forcing: can verifiable geometry improve long-horizon model usefulness?
papers.question: Can a model game these rewards, and do geometric improvements predict closed-loop control gains?

papers.title: RoDyn: Taming Interactive Robot-Dynamic 2.5D World Model for Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Zhang, Chuanrui; Wu, Zhengxian; Lu, Guanxing; Tang, Yansong; Wang, Ziwei
papers.affiliations: Nanyang Technological University; Tsinghua University; Tsinghua Shenzhen International Graduate School, Tsinghua University; Tsinghua University; Nanyang Technological University
papers.summary: RoDyn uses a geometry-aware 2.5D latent representation for robot-environment dynamics. Its tokenizer combines appearance, spatial information, and agent-related priors. Dynamic masks guide autoregressive transitions toward active interaction regions. The authors evaluate both predictive generation and downstream benefits for model-based reinforcement learning and imitation learning.
papers.why: A geometry-aware latent space combines appearance, spatial and agent priors, and masks that focus transitions on interaction regions. A very close match to efficient RGB-D world modeling and your geometry-centric prediction work.
papers.question: Which cost is reduced by 2.5D tokenization, and does masking miss unexpected object interactions?

papers.title: Structure-Preserving Diffusion for Point-Wise 3D Goal State Prediction in Robotic Manipulation
papers.authors: Wang, Dexin; Huan, Hengqiang; Chang, Zhifu; Chang, Faliang; Liu, Chunsheng
papers.affiliations: Shandong University; Shandong University; Shandong University; Shandong University; Shandong University
papers.summary: ForeRobo predicts point-wise 3D goal states using diffusion with structure-preserving constraints. Geometric regularization is intended to keep predicted scene changes usable for manipulation planning. The work connects generative state prediction with a downstream planner instead of predicting only image appearance or directly outputting all motor commands.
papers.why: ForeRobo predicts geometric goal states with structure-preserving constraints, then connects them to planning. A close fit for turning your dense 3D trajectories into actionable predictions.
papers.question: Does the structure loss preserve articulated and deformable motion, or mainly rigid transformations?

papers.title: GAP: Geometric Anchor Pre-Training for Data-Efficient Visuomotor Learning of Manipulation Tasks
papers.authors: Buoso, Davide; Protopapa, Andrea; Di Carlo, Stefano; Pistilli, Francesca; Averta, Giuseppe
papers.affiliations: Politecnico di Torino; Politecnico di Torino; Politecnico di Torino; Politecnico di Torino; Politecnico di Torino
papers.summary: GAP pretrains a small spatial adapter on a simulated proxy task before imitation learning. Object masks encourage sharp, stable keypoints that cover relevant geometry while the visual foundation model remains frozen. Experiments assess whether this inexpensive geometric warm-up reduces overfitting when only a few manipulation demonstrations are available.
papers.why: Uses a lightweight simulated warm-up task to regularize a spatial adapter into stable geometric keypoints while keeping the visual foundation model frozen. A particularly relevant low-cost alternative to adapting the whole encoder.
papers.question: Do geometric gains survive a change in camera, object category, and contact regime?

papers.title: ISF-VLA: An Implicit 3D Vision-Language-Action Model Capitalizing on 3D-Aware Vision Foundation Models through Implicit Spatial Fusion
papers.authors: Zang, Sheng; Wei, Songlin; Geng, Haoran; Tang, Yikai; An, Bo; Senthilnath, J.; Abbeel, Pieter; Malik, Jitendra
papers.affiliations: Nanyang Technological University; University of Southern California; University of California, Berkeley; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; Nanyang Technological University; I2R, ASTAR; UC Berkeley; UC Berkeley
papers.summary: ISF-VLA combines 2D visual features with implicit geometry from a 3D-aware vision model. Cross-attention, camera tokens, and geometric alignment support viewpoint-generalizable manipulation, while token selection limits the extra computation. The authors compare implicit spatial fusion against both 2D-only policies and approaches with explicit 3D inputs.
papers.why: A topical lead on using 3D-aware visual foundations within a VLA. Especially useful after the generalists-versus-specialists panel.
papers.question: How much of the geometry model is necessary at inference, and can its features be distilled?

papers.title: AdaVLA: Adaptive Step Flow Matching for Training-Free Acceleration of Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.authors: Han, Sunghwan; Han, Youngtae; Yi, Youngmin
papers.affiliations: Sogang University; Sogang University; Sogang University
papers.summary: AdaVLA adjusts flow-matching inference without requiring training data. A trajectory-curvature metric guides action-generation step counts, and an importance estimate controls pruning. The work evaluates whether adaptive compute can accelerate several VLA models on embedded hardware while preserving task success.
papers.why: Uses flow-trajectory curvature to adapt step count and pruning without training data. Reports Jetson AGX Orin speedups for π0.5 and X-VLA, plus real-robot validation with SmolVLA. A valuable contrast with Shallow-π and D3P.
papers.question: Does the confidence metric detect hard contacts and out-of-distribution observations, and what is tail latency?

papers.title: SILICA: Repurposing Diffusion Priors for Joint Glass Segmentation and Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Ramakrishnan, Tarun; Verma, Anuj; Nanwani, Laksh; Garg, Sourav; Krishna, Madhava
papers.affiliations: Robotics Research Center, IIIT Hyderabad, India; IIIT Hyderabad; Robotics Research Center, IIIT Hyderabad, India; International Institute of Information Technology Hyderabad (IIITH); IIIT Hyderabad
papers.summary: SILICA repurposes diffusion-model priors to jointly estimate glass segmentation and glass-aware depth. The predicted mask helps remove invalid sensor depth associated with transparent surfaces and recover geometry for mapping and navigation. A dedicated dataset and cross-environment experiments test transfer without paired real-world glass-depth annotations.
papers.why: Uses diffusion priors for transparent-surface segmentation and depth, with a direct connection to ResidualNeRF and your interest in geometry from imperfect depth.
papers.question: Are gains from prior knowledge or explicit physical constraints, and what is the inference budget?

papers.title: ReMAP-DP: Reprojected Multi-View Aligned PointMaps for Diffusion Policy
papers.authors: Yang, XinZhang; Wu, Renjun; Liu, Jinyan; Li, Xuesong
papers.affiliations: Beijing Institute of Technology; Beijing Institute of Technology; Beijing Institute of Technology; Beijing Institute of Technology
papers.summary: ReMAP-DP combines standardized perspective views with pixel-aligned pointmaps in a dual-stream diffusion policy. Learnable modality embeddings fuse semantic features and explicit geometry while preserving patch-level correspondence. Simulation and real manipulation experiments investigate spatial precision, robustness, and learning from a small number of demonstrations.
papers.why: Fuses reprojected views with aligned pointmaps and semantic features. One of the most direct policy-side connections to DUSt3R/MASt3R-style representations.
papers.question: What does explicit pointmap alignment buy over learned implicit geometry, at matched compute?

papers.title: From Flow to One Step: Real-Time Multi-Modal Trajectory Policies Via Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation-Based Distribution Distillation
papers.authors: Dong, Ju; Zhang, Liding; Zhang, Lei; Fu, Yu; Bai, Kaixin; Marton, Zoltan-Csaba; Bing, Zhenshan; Chen, Zhaopeng; Knoll, Alois; Zhang, Jianwei
papers.affiliations: Technical University of Munich; Technical University of Munich; University of Hamburg; Technical University of Munich; University of Hamburg; Agile Robots SE; Technical University of Munich; University of Hamburg; Tech. Univ. Muenchen TUM; University of Hamburg
papers.summary: This method distills a multi-step conditional flow policy into a single-step IMLE student. A bidirectional set-matching objective encourages both accurate trajectories and coverage of multiple action modes. A geometry-aware encoder integrates visual and proprioceptive inputs, and experiments examine high-frequency closed-loop manipulation after distillation.
papers.why: Distills a multi-step flow policy into one step with an objective designed to preserve multiple action modes. The abstract reports 125 Hz versus a 2.9 Hz teacher in its real-world setup. Strong fit for efficient action generation from rich geometry.
papers.question: Does 125 Hz include perception and communication, and how is rare-mode preservation measured?

papers.title: Optical Flow-Guided Manipulation: Learning to Act from Historical and Future Dynamics
papers.authors: Jiang, Yunqing; Chen, Xiangyuan; Qiang, Sunyuan; Liang, Tianlin; IEONG, Chio-In; Liang, Yanyan
papers.affiliations: Macao university of Science and Technology; Macau University of Science and Technology; Macau University of Science and Technology; Guangdong Institute of Intelligence Science and Technology; Guangdong Institute of Intelligence Science and Technology; Macau University of Science and Technology
papers.summary: OFDP conditions a diffusion policy on optical-flow information from ordinary RGB observations. A memory module aggregates historical motion, while a prediction module forecasts future motion cues. This separates understanding scene dynamics from generating actions and is evaluated for data efficiency and robustness in cluttered manipulation scenes.
papers.why: The title and placement make this a useful adjacent talk after one-step distillation, particularly for comparing 2D flow supervision with your 3D tracks.
papers.question: Which failures require 3D geometry rather than optical flow?

papers.title: DreamManip: Holistic Visual Planning for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation via Video Foundation Models
papers.authors: Xiong, Haowen; Zhong, Zhide; Fan, Yusi; Liu, Zhuang; Chen, Wen; Huang, Tianyu; Liu, Jianxing; CHU, Xiaowen; Li, Haoang
papers.affiliations: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou); The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou); Harbin Institute of Technology; Harbin Institute of Technology; Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou); The Chinese University of Hong Kong; Harbin Institute of Technology; The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou); Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou)
papers.summary: DreamManip uses a video foundation model to imagine a visual path from the current observation to a goal image. A robot then executes the generated sequence through visual servoing. This holistic plan is intended to reduce the difficulty of long-horizon manipulation without relying solely on repeated one-step prediction or a final-goal policy.
papers.why: Uses video-model-based visual planning and execution feedback. A useful comparison between long-horizon visual plans and a compact action-conditioned dynamics model.
papers.question: How often must the visual plan be regenerated, and which replanning failures dominate?

papers.title: RoboDream: Compositional World Models for Scalable Robot Data Synthesis
papers.authors: Ye, Junjie; Xue, Rong; Van Hoorick, Basile; Li, Runhao; Belagavi Rajaprakash, Harshitha; Tokmakov, Pavel; Irshad, Muhammad Zubair; Guizilini, Vitor; WANG, YUE
papers.affiliations: University of Southern California; University of Southern California; Toyota Research Institute; University of Southern California; University of Southern California; CMU; Toyota Research Institute; Toyota Research Institute; USC
papers.summary: RoboDream composes robot motion with generated scene and object variation to synthesize manipulation data. Rendered robot motion anchors video generation so that trajectories can be reused as supervision. The work investigates scaling training diversity while preserving a connection between generated images and executable robot behavior.
papers.why: Anchors video generation on robot motion, enabling scene and object variation while retaining trajectory supervision. Directly relevant to your synthetic geometric data and world-action training interests.
papers.question: How is action-label validity checked when generated object dynamics change?

papers.title: IMLE-VLA: Fast Single-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
papers.authors: Hosseinkhani, Kian; Peng, Qinhe; Shramko, George; Aghabozorgi, Mehran; Qian, Jianing; Engst, Tristan; Moazeni, Alireza; Jayaraman, Dinesh; Li, Ke
papers.affiliations: Simon Fraser University; university of pennsylvania; Simon Fraser University; Simon Fraser University; University of Pennsylvania; Simon Fraser University; Simon Fraser University; University of Pennsylvania; Simon Fraser University
papers.summary: IMLE-VLA replaces a VLA’s iterative diffusion or flow action head with a single-step conditional generator. Its conditional IMLE objective is designed to preserve multiple plausible action modes. Evaluations compare task success, robustness, inference speed, and physical robot motion against the original multi-step policy.
papers.why: Replaces iterative diffusion/flow action sampling with a single-step conditional IMLE head while retaining multimodal action coverage. A particularly useful student-author conversation before comparing Wednesday’s one-step distillation paper.
papers.question: What remains expensive after replacing the action head, and how does the training cost compare with distillation?

papers.title: Compositional Average Velocity Modeling for Efficient Diffusion Offline Reinforcement Learning
papers.authors: Nguyen, Thanh; Syarubany, Abu Hanif Muhammad; Kim, Hwanhee; Yoo, Chang D.
papers.leadAuthors: Nguyen, Thanh;  Syarubany, Abu Hanif Muhammad
papers.affiliations: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology (KAIST); Korea Advanced Institute of Science & Technology; KAIST; KAIST
papers.summary: InsQL learns a direct noise-to-action mapping using compositional average-velocity modeling. It integrates the one-step generative policy with behavior-regularized actor-critic optimization, avoiding a separate teacher-distillation stage. Offline reinforcement-learning and robot experiments examine both training efficiency and action-generation cost, with optional value-guided candidate selection.
papers.why: InsQL learns a direct noise-to-action policy without a separate distillation stage. A good comparison for whether a one-step objective is preferable to compressing a pretrained generative policy.
papers.question: How does value-guided candidate selection change the claimed single-step inference budget?

papers.title: Generalizable Robotic Insertion with World Models
papers.authors: Hansen, Nicklas; Akinola, Iretiayo; Guo, Yijie; Xu, Jie; Tang, Bingjie; Su, Hao; Wang, Xiaolong; Gupta, Abhishek; Fox, Dieter; Narang, Yashraj
papers.affiliations: University of California San Diego; NVIDIA; Nvidia; NVIDIA; University of Southern California; UC San Diego; UC San Diego; University of Washington; University of Washington; NVIDIA
papers.summary: This insertion system learns a visual and proprioceptive world model across many part geometries. The model supports manipulation of previously unseen objects and can be fine-tuned for new tasks. Experiments compare zero-shot transfer and adaptation efficiency with specialized or model-free alternatives in contact-rich assembly.
papers.why: A visual/proprioceptive world model trained across diverse insertion geometries transfers to unseen parts. This is a concrete contact-rich test of whether learned dynamics provide generalization and adaptation benefits.
papers.question: What state captures contact, how expensive is planning, and what changes when geometry is out of distribution?
